english: The just man, and tenacious of his purpose,
note: virum is object of quatit (line 4); propositi: genitive with tenacem, 'of resolve'; 'his' supplied.

english: not the ardour of citizens ordering crooked things,
note: prava iubentium: urging (commanding) wrong, lit. crooked, things. non ... non ... neque ... nec (lines 2-6) kept where they stand.

english: not the face of a pressing tyrant
note: voltus: countenance; instantis: pressing, menacing.

english: shakes in his solid mind, nor Auster,
note: mente ... solida: ablative, 'in (from) his firm mind'; 'his' supplied. Auster: the south wind.

english: the turbulent leader of the restless Hadria,
note: Hadria (masc.): the Adriatic sea; the south wind as its 'leader', i.e. its master who stirs it.

english: nor the great hand of lightning-hurling Jove:
if, broken, the round world should slip down upon him,
note: orbis: the round, the world (or vault of heaven); inlabatur: present subjunctive, 'should fall in (upon him)'; 'upon him' renders the prefix in-.

english: the ruins will strike him unafraid.
note: inpavidum: accusative, him (the just man) unafraid.

latin: hac arte Pollux et vagus Hercules
english: By this art Pollux and wandering Hercules,
note: hac arte: by this quality (steadfastness), lit. art.

english: having striven upward, reached the fiery citadels,
note: enisus: having struggled up; attigit singular with the nearer subject; arcis igneas: the fiery heights of heaven (the stars).

english: among whom Augustus, reclining,
note: quos inter: anastrophe, 'between whom'.

english: with purple mouth will drink nectar;
note: bibet (Shorey), future; variant bibit noted. purpureo: purple, i.e. glowing (with divine youth).

latin: hac te merentem, Bacche pater, tuae
english: by this you, deserving, Bacchus father, your
note: hac (arte): by this (quality).

english: tigers carried, the yoke with untaught
note: vexere: perfect, 'carried'; iugum is object of trahentes (line 15); indocili collo: on an unteachable neck.

english: neck drawing; by this Quirinus
note: Quirinus: the deified Romulus.

english: on the horses of Mars fled Acheron,
note: Acheronta: Greek accusative; fugit: perfect, 'escaped' the river of the dead.

english: a pleasing thing having spoken out to the deliberating
note: gratum elocuta ... Iunone (line 18): ablative absolute, 'Juno having spoken (something) welcome'.

english: Juno, to the gods: “Ilion, Ilion
note: Quotation marks as in the source text: Juno's speech runs to line 68.

english: a fateful and unchaste judge
note: fatalis incestusque iudex: Paris, the judge of the goddesses.

english: and a foreign woman has turned
note: mulier peregrina: Helen; vertit: perfect, singular with the nearer subject, 'has overturned'.

latin: in pulverem ex quo destituit deos
english: into dust, from the time when defrauded the gods
note: ex quo: since; destituit: left in the lurch, cheated; subject Laomedon (line 22).

english: of the bargained wage Laomedon, to me
note: mercede pacta: ablative, of the agreed pay (for building Troy's walls); mihi: dative of agent with damnatum.

english: and to chaste Minerva condemned,
note: damnatum agrees with Ilion (line 18).

english: with its people and its deceitful leader.
note: 'its' supplied (twice); duce fraudulento: Laomedon.

english: Now neither for the Laconian adulteress gleams
note: Lacaenae ... adulterae: dative, the Spartan woman, Helen; nec ... nec (lines 25-26) kept in place.

english: the infamous guest, nor the house of Priam
note: famosus hospes: Paris; splendet: gleams (in finery).

english: perjured the combative Achivi
note: periura agrees with domus; Achivos (the Achaeans) is object of refringit.

english: with Hectorean resources breaks back,
note: Hectoreis opibus: with Hector's might (power); refringit: breaks, beats back.

english: and, by our dissensions drawn out,
note: nostris seditionibus: the gods' own quarrels; ductum: prolonged, agrees with bellum.

english: the war has settled down; forthwith both the heavy
note: resedit: perfect, has subsided; et ... et: both ... and.

english: angers and the hated grandson,
note: nepotem: Romulus, son of Mars (Juno's son) and Ilia.

english: whom the Trojan priestess bore,
note: Troica sacerdos: Ilia (Rhea Silvia), descended from Aeneas.

english: to Mars I shall give up; him I to the shining
note: redonabo: I shall give back (remit, forgive for Mars's sake).

english: seats to enter, to learn of nectar
note: lucidas ... sedes: the bright seats (of heaven).

english: the juices, and to be enrolled in the tranquil
note: sucos: juices, i.e. the drink; adscribi: be enrolled (as a citizen).

english: ranks of the gods I shall allow.
note: patiar: future, 'I shall suffer (allow)'.

english: As long as, long, between should rage Ilion
note: dum ... saeviat: present subjunctive; longus ... pontus: a long sea between Ilion and Rome.

english: and Rome the sea, in whatever, as exiles,
note: qualibet ... in parte: in any part whatever; exsules: as exiles.

english: part let them reign, blessed;
note: regnanto: future imperative, 3rd plural; subject the descendants of Troy (the Romans).

english: while on the tomb of Priam and of Paris
note: busto: dative with insultet.

english: should prance the herd, and the wild beasts their cubs
note: insultet: leap on, trample (in scorn); ferae (subject) and catulos (object) set in English order within the line.

english: should hide unpunished, let the Capitol stand
note: inultae: unpunished, with impunity; stet: jussive subjunctive.

english: gleaming, and, on the triumphed-over, may
note: triumphatis ... Medis (line 44): dative, the Medes led in triumph; possit: may (be able).

english: Rome fierce give laws, to the Medes.
note: dare iura: give laws (impose terms).

english: Dreadful far and wide, her name to the farthest
note: horrenda: nominative, agrees with Roma; 'her' supplied.

english: let her extend shores, where the middle liquid
note: in ultimas ... oras (lines 45-46): to the farthest shores; medius liquor: the intervening water (the Mediterranean, the straits).

english: separates Europe from the African,
note: Europen: Greek accusative; Afro: the African (man or land), i.e. Africa.

english: where the swollen Nile waters the fields.
note: rigat: waters, irrigates (with the flood).

latin: aurum inrepertum et sic melius situm,
english: Gold undiscovered and so better placed
note: inrepertum: not found; situm: laid, placed.

english: when the earth hides it, braver at spurning
note: fortior (Roma): stronger, braver to spurn; 'it' supplied.

english: than at gathering into human uses
note: cogere: to collect, force together.

english: with a right hand seizing everything sacred,
note: omne sacrum rapiente dextra: ablative absolute, plundering all that is holy.

english: whatever limit has stood in the world's way,
note: mundo: dative, 'has stood against the world'; obstitit: perfect.

english: this she will touch with arms, eager to visit
note: tanget: future; gestiens: longing, eager.

english: in which part fires may rage like Bacchants,
note: qua parte: in what region; debacchentur: subjunctive, rave in Bacchic frenzy (metaphor: the torrid zone).

english: in which clouds and rainy dews.
note: Verb understood from line 55; the clouds and rains of the frozen north.

english: But to the warlike Quirites the fates
note: Quiritibus: the Roman citizens.

latin: hac lege dico, ne nimium pii
english: on this condition I declare, lest, too much dutiful
note: hac lege: by this law, condition; ne: lest (negative purpose), kept where it stands; pii: devoted, dutiful (to Troy).

english: and trusting in their fortunes, of ancestral
note: rebus: circumstances, prosperity; avitae ... Troiae: of their grandfathers' Troy.

english: roofs they should wish to restore, Troy.
note: tecta: roofs, i.e. houses; Troiae: genitive with tecta and avitae, 'of ancestral Troy'.

english: Of Troy, reborn under a mournful bird,
note: alite lugubri: with a bird of ill omen (augury).

english: the fortune with sad slaughter shall be repeated,
note: fortuna Troiae renascens (line 61); iterabitur: future passive.

english: leading the victorious bands
note: ducente ... me (line 64): ablative absolute, 'I leading'.

english: I, wife of Jove and sister.
note: coniuge me Iovis et sorore: ablative absolute, me being the wife and sister of Jove.

english: Thrice if should rise again the bronze wall
note: resurgat ... pereat ... ploret: present subjunctives, future less vivid condition.

english: with Phoebus as founder, thrice would it perish, by my
note: auctore Phoebo: ablative absolute, with Phoebus (Apollo) as builder.

english: Argives cut down, thrice would the wife,
note: excisus: razed, cut down; meis Argivis: my Argives, the Greeks.

english: captured, her husband and boys bewail.”
note: virum: her husband; 'her' supplied. Closing quotation mark as in the source.

english: This will not suit a jesting lyre —
note: conveniet: future.

english: whither, Muse, are you heading? Cease, wilful one,
note: tendis: you are straining, going; pervicax: obstinate, vocative.

english: to report the talk of the gods and
note: sermones: conversations, discourses.

english: great things with small measures to make thin.
note: modis: measures, strains; tenuare: to thin, diminish.

latin: Descende caelo et dic age tibia
english: Come down from the sky and speak, come, on the pipe,
note: age: come! (imperative interjection); tibia: ablative, with (on) the reed pipe.

english: queen Calliope, a long melody,
note: regina: vocative; melos: Greek neuter, song, melody.

english: whether with voice now you prefer high,
note: voce ... acuta: with a high, clear voice.

english: or with strings or the cithara of Phoebus.
note: fidibus: lyre strings; citharave: or the cithara (lyre).

english: Do you hear? Or does there mock me a lovable
note: auditis: plural, addressed to the company; ludit: mocks, deceives.

english: madness? I seem both to hear and, holy,
note: audire et videor ... errare: 'I seem to hear and to wander'; pios ... lucos: sacred groves.

english: to wander through groves, which pleasant
note: amoenae agrees with aquae et aurae (line 8).

latin: quos et aquae subeunt et aurae.
english: both waters and breezes come beneath.
note: quos ... subeunt: steal into (pass under) the groves.

english: Me, the fabled ones, on Vultur in Apulia,
note: fabulosae: nominative plural with palumbes (line 12), storied, legendary; Volture: Mount Vultur.

english: outside the threshold of the nurse Pullia
note: Text doubtful: Pulliae (Shorey) is a conjecture; the manuscripts repeat Apuliae (after Apulo), which gives a metrical anomaly. Rendered as the source reads.

english: with play and wearied with sleep
note: ludo fatigatumque somno: wearied by play and by sleep.

english: with fresh foliage, a boy, the wood-doves
note: puerum: me as a boy; palumbes: subject of texere.

english: covered, a wonder which would be to all
note: texere: perfect, 'covered'; mirum quod foret: a marvel to be to all.

english: whoever of lofty Acerontia the nest
note: Aceruntia (Acherontia): a hill town in Apulia/Lucania, perched like a nest.

english: and the Bantine glades and the field
note: saltus Bantinos: the woodland pastures of Bantia.

english: rich hold, of low-lying Forentum,
note: humilis Forenti: of low Forentum; 'hold' = inhabit.

latin: ut tuto ab atris corpore viperis
english: how, with body safe from black vipers
note: ut: how, that; tuto ... corpore: ablative absolute, 'with my body safe'.

latin: dormirem et ursis, ut premerer sacra
english: I slept, and bears; how I was heaped with sacred
note: dormirem: subjunctive; ab ... viperis ... et ursis: from vipers and bears; premerer: was covered over.

english: laurel and with myrtle gathered together,
not without the gods a spirited infant.
note: non sine dis: litotes kept, 'not without the gods'.

english: Yours, Camenae, yours, into the steep
note: Camenae: the Italian Muses; vester: 'your (man)', i.e. yours.

english: Sabines I am lifted, or whether to me cool
note: in arduos Sabinos: into the steep Sabine hills; seu mihi ... placuere: whether ... have pleased me.

english: Praeneste or sloping Tibur
note: supinum: lying back, sloping.

english: or clear Baiae have pleased.
note: liquidae: clear (of air or water); placuere: perfect.

english: To your springs and dances a friend,
note: amicum agrees with me (line 26); choris: choirs, dances.

latin: non me Philippis versa acies retro,
english: not me at Philippi the battle line turned back,
note: versa acies retro: the line turned back (the rout at Philippi, 42 BC); verb extinxit in line 27.

english: the accursed tree did not extinguish,
note: non stands with extinxit in the Latin; devota arbor: the tree that nearly fell on Horace (Odes 2.13).

english: nor Palinurus with Sicilian wave.
note: Palinurus: the cape off Lucania; Sicula unda: the sea toward Sicily.

english: Whenever with me you will be, gladly
note: utcumque: whenever.

english: the raving, as a sailor, Bosporus
note: insanientem: raging; navita: as a sailor.

english: I shall try, and the burning sands
note: temptabo: I shall attempt, venture on.

english: of the Assyrian shore, as a traveller;
I shall visit the Britons, to strangers fierce,
note: hospitibus: to guests, strangers (who are sacrificed).

english: and the Concanian glad with horse's blood,
note: Concanum: of the Concani, a Cantabrian tribe in Spain said to drink horse blood.

english: I shall visit the quivered Geloni
note: Gelonos: a Scythian people.

english: and the Scythian, unharmed, river.
note: inviolatus: inviolate (of the speaker); amnem: the river Tanais (Don).

english: You lofty Caesar, as soon as, by warfare
note: simul: as soon as; militia: ablative, with fessas (line 38).

english: the tired cohorts he has stowed in towns,
note: abdidit: has hidden away, settled (veterans in colonies).

english: seeking to end his labours,
note: 'his' supplied.

english: in the Pierian cave refresh.
note: Pierio antro: the Muses' grotto; recreatis: present.

latin: vos lene consilium et datis et dato
english: You gentle counsel both give and, it given,
note: dato (consilio): ablative with gaudetis, 'rejoice in it, given'.

english: rejoice, kindly ones. We know how the impious
note: almae: vocative, nurturing (Muses); ut: how.

english: Titans and the monstrous crowd
note: immanem turbam: the Giants.

english: with falling thunderbolt he took away
note: sustulerit: perfect subjunctive (indirect question), removed, destroyed; caduco: falling.

latin: qui terram inertem, qui mare temperat
english: who the inert earth, who the sea governs
note: qui ... temperat: Jupiter; temperat: tempers, governs.

english: windy, and cities and kingdoms sad
note: regna tristia: the gloomy realms (of the underworld).

english: and gods and mortal troops
note: turmas: squadrons, i.e. throngs.

english: with fair command rules alone.
note: unus: alone; aequo: even, just.

english: Great terror that had brought upon Jove,
note: illa (line 49) agrees with iuventus (line 50): 'that youth'.

english: confident youth, bristling with arms,
note: horrida bracchiis: bristling with (many) arms, the hundred-handed; fidens: trusting (in their strength).

english: and the brothers, straining, on shadowy
note: fratres: the Aloadae, Otus and Ephialtes; tendentes: striving.

english: Pelion to have set on Olympus.
note: inposuisse: perfect infinitive, to have placed; opaco ... Olympo: on shady Olympus.

latin: sed quid Typhoeus et validus Mimas
english: But what Typhoeus and strong Mimas,
or what Porphyrion with threatening stance,
note: statu: posture, stance.

english: what Rhoetus, and with uprooted trunks
note: evolsis truncis: trees torn up.

english: Enceladus, bold javelin-thrower,
against the sounding aegis of Pallas
note: aegida: Greek accusative.

english: could do, rushing? On this side eager stood
note: possent: imperfect subjunctive (deliberative); hinc ... hinc: on this side ... on that.

english: Volcanus, on that side matron Juno, and
note: matrona: the matron (wife of Jove).

english: never from his shoulders about to lay down his bow
note: numquam ... positurus: never going to lay aside; 'his' supplied (twice).

english: he who with pure dew of Castalia washes
note: lavit: present (lavere), 'washes'; rore ... Castaliae: water of the Castalian spring.

english: his loosened hair, who of Lycia holds
note: crinis solutos: flowing hair; 'his' supplied.

english: the thickets and his native wood,
note: natalem silvam: the wood of his birth (on Delos); 'his' supplied.

english: the Delian and Pataraean Apollo.
note: Patareus: of Patara in Lycia.

latin: vis consili expers mole ruit sua,
english: Force without counsel falls by its own mass;
note: consili expers: having no share of wisdom; mole sua: by its own weight.

english: force tempered the gods also carry forward
note: vim temperatam (object) ... di (subject): the gods also advance controlled force.

english: into greater; the same hate forces
note: in maius: to greater (heights); idem: the same (gods), nominative plural; viris: accusative plural of vis, strengths.

english: every wickedness in mind setting in motion.
note: moventis agrees with viris; animo: in the mind (in intention).

english: Witness of my, the hundred-handed Gyas,
note: testis: (is) witness; mearum ... sententiarum (line 70): of my opinions; Gyas (Gyges): one of the hundred-handed.

english: opinions, and the known, of untouched,
note: notus ... temptator (line 71): the notorious assailant; integrae ... Dianae: of virgin Diana.

english: assailant Orion, of Diana,
note: temptator: attempter, assailant.

english: by a virgin arrow subdued.
note: domitus: tamed, subdued.

english: Laid upon her own monsters, Earth grieves
note: iniecta: thrown upon; suis: her own (offspring, the Giants buried beneath her).

english: and mourns her offspring, by the thunderbolt, lurid,
note: partus: offspring, accusative plural; 'her' supplied; luridum ... Orcum (line 75): pale Orcus.

english: sent to Orcus; nor has eaten through
note: missos ad Orcum: sent to Orcus (the underworld); peredit: has eaten up (perfect).

english: the swift fire Aetna, set upon them,
note: ignis (subject) peredit Aetnen (object, Greek accusative) inpositam: Aetna laid upon (the buried Giant); 'them' supplied.

english: nor the liver of lustful Tityos
note: nec stands second in the Latin line (incontinentis nec Tityi iecur), negating reliquit; incontinentis: unrestrained, lustful.

english: has the bird left, to his wickedness assigned
note: ales: the bird (vulture); nequitiae additus custos: set as guard over his lewdness; 'his' supplied.

english: as guard; the lover, three hundred
note: amatorem ... Pirithoum (line 80): object; trecentae ... catenae: subject.

english: chains hold back, Pirithous.
note: Pirithous, who tried to carry off Proserpina; cohibent: restrain.

english: Jove thundering in heaven we have believed
note: credidimus: perfect; caelo: in the sky (or 'from the sky').

english: to reign; a present god will be held
note: praesens divus: a god manifest (on earth).

english: Augustus, the Britons having been added
note: adiectis Britannis ... Persis: ablative absolute.

english: to the empire, and the heavy Persians.
note: gravibus: grievous, oppressive; Persis: the Parthians.

english: Has the soldier of Crassus, with a barbarian wife
note: milesne: -ne interrogative; Crassus's men captured at Carrhae, 53 BC.

english: a base husband, lived, and of enemies,
note: hostium (line 6) with socerorum (line 8): of enemy fathers-in-law.

english: O senate-house and morals turned upside down!
note: pro: alas for; inversi mores: overturned customs.

english: grown old, of fathers-in-law, in the arms
note: consenuit: has grown old; in armis: in the service (arms) of.

latin: sub rege Medo Marsus et Apulus,
english: under a Median king, the Marsian and the Apulian,
note: Medo: Median, i.e. Parthian.

english: of the Ancilia and the name and the toga
note: anciliorum: the sacred shields of Mars kept by the Salii.

english: forgetful, and of eternal Vesta,
note: oblitus: having forgotten.

english: with Jove unharmed and the city Rome?
note: incolumi Iove et urbe Roma: ablative absolute, Jove (his Capitol) and Rome standing safe.

english: This the foreseeing mind of Regulus had guarded against
note: caverat: pluperfect; provida: provident.

english: dissenting from the conditions
note: condicionibus: terms (of the exchange of prisoners).

english: foul, and from the precedent drawing
note: trahentis (Shorey): genitive with Reguli, 'of (him) drawing'; many editors read trahenti, dative with exemplo; exemplo: from the precedent.

english: ruin into the coming age,
note: perniciem: ruin (object of trahentis); veniens in aevum: into the age to come (veniens neuter accusative with aevum).

english: if not should perish unpitied
note: si non periret: if (it) should not perish; inmiserabilis: unpitied.

english: the captive youth. “Standards I on Punic
note: Quotation marks as in the source: Regulus's speech, lines 18-40.

english: fastened to shrines, and arms
note: delubris: temples.

english: from soldiers without slaughter,” he said,
note: sine caede: without bloodshed (surrendered); quotation marks as in source.

english: “torn away, I have seen; I have seen, I, of citizens
note: derepta: stripped off; quotation mark as in source.

english: twisted back on a free back the arms
note: retorta tergo bracchia libero: arms bound back behind a free(born) back.

english: and gates not closed, and fields
being tilled, ravaged by our Mars.
note: Marte ... nostro: by our Mars (metaphor: by our warfare); coli: present passive infinitive.

english: With gold bought back, of course, keener
note: scilicet: no doubt (ironic); repensus: ransomed, lit. weighed back.

english: the soldier will return! To disgrace you add
note: flagitio: to the shameful act; additis: you add.

english: loss; neither lost colours
note: neque ... nec (lines 27-29) kept in place.

english: does the wool bring back, dyed with dye,
note: medicata fuco: treated (doctored) with dye (orchil).

latin: nec vera virtus, cum semel excidit,
english: nor true virtue, when once it has fallen away,
note: excidit: has slipped out (been lost).

english: cares to be put back in the worse.
note: deterioribus: dative, in (for) the degenerate.

english: If fights, disentangled from thick
note: extricata densis ... plagis: freed from close-meshed nets.

english: nets, a hind, he will be brave
note: erit ille fortis: that man will be brave.

english: who to faithless enemies entrusted himself,
note: perfidis: treacherous (the Carthaginians).

english: and the Poeni with Mars a second will crush;
note: Marte altero: in a second war (metaphor: Mars = war); Poenos: Carthaginians.

english: who the thongs on his bound arms
note: lora: straps; restrictis lacertis: arms tied back; 'his' supplied.

english: felt, inert, and feared death.
note: iners: spiritless.

english: This man, whence he should take life unknowing,
note: inscius unde vitam sumeret: not knowing from where (how) he should take life (survival).

english: has mixed peace with war. O shame!
note: duello: archaic for bello.

english: O great Carthage, by the disgraceful
note: probrosis ... ruinis (line 40): by the shameful downfall.

english: higher by the ruins of Italy!”
note: altior: taller, raised up; ruinis: ablative (of cause or comparison); closing quotation mark as in source.

english: He is said of his chaste wife the kiss
note: fertur: is said; 'his' supplied.

english: and his little children, as one lessened in status,
note: capitis minor: diminished in civil status (capitis deminutio, as a captive); 'his' supplied.

english: from himself to have put away, and his manly
note: 'his' supplied.

english: grim, on the ground to have set, face,
note: torvus: grimly, nominative; virilem ... voltum: object.

english: until the wavering, by counsel, fathers
note: labantis ... patres: the faltering senators; consilio ... dato (line 46): by counsel never given at another time.

english: he should strengthen as author, never otherwise given,
note: auctor: as proposer; numquam alias dato agrees with consilio (line 45).

english: and amid grieving friends
an outstanding exile should hasten.
note: egregius: distinguished; properaret: subjunctive.

english: And yet he knew what for him the barbarian
note: atqui: and yet; sibi: for himself.

english: torturer was preparing; not otherwise, however,
note: non aliter ... quam (line 53): not otherwise than.

english: he moved aside the opposing kinsmen
note: obstantis: standing in the way.

english: and the people delaying his return
note: reditus: (his) going back, accusative plural; 'his' supplied.

english: than if of clients the long business,
note: clientum longa negotia: the long cases of his clients.

english: the suit decided, he were leaving,
note: diiudicata lite: ablative absolute.

english: heading for the Venafran fields
note: tendens: making for; Venafrum: country town in Campania.

english: or Lacedaemonian Tarentum.
note: Lacedaemonium: Tarentum was founded from Sparta.
